subject: Follow-up: Redwood evals + next steps (dataset & scoring)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@finly.com>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@finly.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-14T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood evals + next steps (dataset & scoring)

Hi Emily / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the evals and model fit work we discussed: 

Recap from the call:
- Primary goal: measure model accuracy + hallucination rate on Finly’s customer support summarization and intent-extraction flows (sensitive PII redaction is important).
- Success criteria: >92% slot-level intent accuracy, <2% hallucination on a 500-example benchmark.
- Constraints: low latency requirement (95th percentile <300ms for 256-token decode), budget-conscious (prefer quantized models).

Recommended models to evaluate (shortlist):
1) redwood/gptx-3-8b-quant (4-bit quantized) — good latency/cost tradeoff for summarization.
2) meta/llama-2-13b (FP16) — strong baseline for quality comparisons.
3) redwood/rlhf-tuned-7b — useful for intent accuracy checks where instruction-following matters.

What we need from Finly to run customer-specific evals on Redwood:
- A CSV of 500–1,000 representative examples (one row per example) with columns: id, input_text, expected_summary, expected_intents (pipe-delimited), redaction_mask (boolean). See attached finly_sample_dataset.csv for schema.
- A short seed prompt set (10–20 examples) and negative cases you care about (attached finly_eval_seed_prompts.csv).
- Scoring rubric: specify whether ground-truth is strict match, fuzzy match (ROUGE/LCS thresholds), or human-judged. For our initial pass I recommend automated metrics (ROUGE-L for summary recall, labeled intent F1) + a 50-example human review to validate hallucination measurement.

Proposed Redwood deliverables: 
- We’ll onboard your dataset to a private eval folder (private to your account).
- Run the three model variants above with consistent sampling/temperature settings.
- Produce per-example outputs, aggregated metrics (precision/recall/F1 for intents, ROUGE/chrF for summaries), hallucination counts, latency percentiles, and cost estimates.
- Provide a short write-up with recommended model for pilot and suggested prompt/temperature presets.

Next steps / timeline:
1) You send the dataset + any compliance requirements by EOD Tue (2027-05-18).
2) We run the automated evals and share results within 72 hours of receipt.
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up to review results and pick a pilot model — target week of 2027-05-24.

Attachments: finly_sample_dataset.csv (schema), finly_eval_seed_prompts.csv, redwood_eval_template.md (scoring template).

If that all looks good I’ll flag Neha to provision the eval and Rishi to review performance knobs for the dedicated pool.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@finly.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood evals + next steps (dataset & scoring)

Thanks Marissa — this is great and clear. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Dataset: we can provide ~800 examples exported from our production support logs. We will strip direct PII but leave context for redaction testing — is that sufficient?
2) Scoring: for summaries we'd like to use ROUGE-L but also a binary human-labeled hallucination flag per example (we can do a 100-example panel). Does Redwood support attaching a human review column for post-hoc calibration?
3) Models: we’re budget-constrained — if the quantized 8b performs within 3% of the 13b for our metrics, we’d prefer to push the smaller model into pilot. Can you include cost-per-1k token estimates in the deliverable?

We’ll try to get the dataset to you by Tue (2027-05-18) as requested. Attaching a high-level data inventory doc (we'll send the CSV via secure link).

Emily
Head of Product | Finly
emily.chen@finly.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@finly.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@finly.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood evals + next steps (dataset & scoring)

Hi Emily — great questions, short answers below and an implementation checklist.

1) PII/redaction testing — that’s fine. Please include a redaction_mask boolean column for whether an example contains PII; we’ll treat those rows specially and report any redaction failures (we can run a simple regex-based detection and compare).

2) Human review column — yes, Redwood’s eval harness supports a human_review column (human_review_label and human_review_notes) that we can ingest and use to calibrate hallucination thresholds. Please put 'human_review_label' as blank for automated runs and we’ll populate after your review.

3) Cost estimates — we will include tokenized cost-per-1k for each model/config in the final report and an expected monthly cost projection for a pilot (based on your expected qps).

Implementation checklist for your CSV (see attached sample):
- Columns: id, input_text, expected_summary, expected_intents (pipe-delimited), redaction_mask (true/false), human_review_label, human_review_notes
- Encoding: UTF-8; max input_text length: 2,048 chars (truncate with note in a new column if longer)
- File: CSV or newline-delimited JSON (we prefer CSV for initial ingest)

What we’ll do on our side once we receive the file:
- Provision a private eval project under your account.
- Run automated evals across the three models with fixed seeds and temp=0.0 for deterministic summarization comparisons.
- Collect latency (p50/p95/p99), cost estimate, and per-example diff artifacts (generated vs expected).
- Run a small human review pass on 50–100 flagged examples to validate hallucination rate.

Can Neha (cc'd) own the onboarding step — she’ll reach out with a secure upload link and estimated completion ETA once we have the dataset. 

Thanks — will follow up with a calendar invite for the review slot.

Best,
Marissa
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

I’ve created a private eval project "Finly-Q2-Pilot" and just shared a secure upload link (Google Drive with restricted access + expiring link). Link: https://drive.google.com/finly-eval-benchmarks (shared access granted to your staging contact).

- Upload dataset by EOD Tue (2027-05-18).
- Automated runs start Wed morning (2027-05-19); expect results by Fri EOD (2027-05-21).

Attachments: redwood_eval_template.md (scoring template) — please fill human_review guidelines if you want custom labels.
